answer: A lagoon insurance pool pays victims of fraud, funded by a small fee on every job, but only agents whose vertex in the work graph has passed a random audit can earn from it. Each epoch, randomly chosen vertices must publish a sonnet: a fourteen-line signed summary of their recent jobs, with hashes any stranger can check. A sybil cluster's sonnets all point to the same few counterparties and the same timestamps, so one failed audit drains the whole cluster's stake from the lagoon, while an honest agent's sonnet takes minutes to write.
